subject: Compute entitlement reconciliation and burst-safety for GraniteAI POC
messages:
From: Amit Patel <amit@granite.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@granite.ai>
Date: 2028-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GraniteAI POC profile and peak patterns

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — GraniteAI is excited to move the POC forward. Attached is a simple CSV export of our request traces (short and long gen mixes) and the expected traffic pattern for the first 90 days. Key notes:
- Baseline steady-state: ~280k tokens/day (~3.2 TPS average over 24h).
- Peak bursts: up to 700 TPS sustained for ~2–5 minutes during business hours (billing events).
- Long-tail completions: 20% of requests are heavy (1.5k tokens average per request), 80% are short (~60 tokens).

SLO target: 95th-percentile latency under 350ms for the short path, and under 1.2s for long completions.

Can you confirm if Dedicated capacity can meet this with a 20% safety buffer? Also please advise on our suggested commit level for the POC vs production.

Attachments: granite_workload_profile.csv (trace export, 3 columns: timestamp, tokens, request_type)

—Amit
Amit Patel
Head of Platform
GraniteAI

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@granite.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GraniteAI POC profile and peak patterns

Amit — thanks for the data and the clear SLOs. I pulled the CSV and did a quick pass; summarized findings below. PDF proposal attached with options.

Quick summary (high level):
- Workload mix: 80% short (avg 60 tokens), 20% long (avg 1500 tokens).
- Observed instantaneous peak in sample: ~680 TPS for ~3 minutes (matches your note).

Sizing assumptions we used for Dedicated sizing:
1) Model: g-redwood-7b-q4f (optimized for throughput)
2) Short-path token throughput per GPU (sustained, 1 GPU): ~2,500 tokens/sec for short completions (low-latency path).
3) Long-path token throughput per GPU: ~600 tokens/sec (heavy attention/kv cache usage).
4) We reserve one GPU per 700 TPS short-request-equivalent for tail safety calculations.

Baseline compute recommendation (POC):
- Commit: 6 GPUs dedicated (g-pool units) — this maps to ~15k tokens/sec short-path capacity (headroom ~2.2x over observed peak short mix).
- Expected P95 latency: short path ~280–320ms, long path ~850–1,100ms.
- Safety buffer: ~20–30% headroom for burst absorption and prewarming.

Production guidance (if GraniteAI moves to full prod):
- Commit range: 12–18 GPUs depending on growth assumptions (see PDF for ramp/commit scenarios).
- Autoscale/burst: allow burst capacity of +30% ephemeral GPUs for multi-minute spikes; we can route to pre-warmed pools to maintain SLOs.

Open items / asks for you:
- Confirm the long-request percentage remains ~20% across business-critical windows.
- Any constraints around run-of-the-mill cold starts or model changes during the POC?

I'll flag this to Steph and Ben to validate the kernel-level throughput numbers — they may tune the recommendation slightly (quantization profile / batching tweak).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

[attachment: granite_compute_proposal.pdf (proposal + 3 commit scenarios)]

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Amit Patel <amit@granite.ai>
Date: 2028-06-22T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GraniteAI POC profile and peak patterns

Looping in a couple of kernel / ops notes — ran the trace through our throughput estimator and stress rules. My adjustments below.

Important math (engineer's quick take):
- Effective TPS conversion: short requests (avg 60 tokens) => each req costs ~60 tokens. At 680 TPS requests that's ~40.8k tokens/sec.
- Our short-path throughput per A100-equivalent GPU (mixed batching, continuous KV): ~22k tokens/sec when optimized (q4f + fused kernels). That implies peak short-path load could be handled by 2 GPUs at raw token rate.
- However, long requests (1.5k tokens) create KV pressure and heat steady-state; effective tokens/sec drops to ~5k tokens/sec per GPU for long-path heavy windows.
- For a mixed peak (20% long), aggregate tokens/sec at 680 TPS -> 0.8*680*60 + 0.2*680*1500 = 32,640 + 204,000 = 236,640 tokens/sec aggregate.

Recommendation update (ops-safe):
- Minimum Dedicated for POC: 10 GPUs (A100-eq), provisioned as 8 committed + 2 burst — gives ~~(8*22k + 2*5k)=186k + 10k = 196k tokens/sec nominal. We still have a shortfall to the computed peak above because the customer peak is token-heavy.
- To consistently meet 95p latency SLOs on mixed peak, we propose either:
  a) Reduce long-request concurrency during peaks via gating (recommended) and keep 10 GPUs; or
  b) Increase commit to 14 GPUs to cover heavy-token spikes without gating.

SLO tradeoffs:
- With gating (a), short-path latency will stay comfortably under 350ms; long-path completions will queue with graceful backlog and degraded p95 but still finish within 2–3s.
- With larger commit (b), both short and long stay within target SLOs but increases monthly committed spend ~40%.

I'll prepare a simple TCO comparison (commit 8/10/14) and include operational options (gating rules, prewarm windows).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Patel <amit@granite.ai>, Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@granite.ai>
Date: 2028-06-23T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GraniteAI POC profile and peak patterns — proposed ask to customer

Team / Amit — thanks for the quick analysis everyone. Lauren, Ben: great work surfacing token-based shortfall. Proposed next steps to present to GraniteAI tomorrow:

1) Present two binding options in the POC proposal (slide + appendix):
   - Option A (Cost-conservative): 8 committed GPUs with burst pool up to +30% and request gating during top 1% minutes. Expected to meet short SLOs; long-path p95 may extend to 2–3s under extreme peaks.
   - Option B (Performance-first): 14 committed GPUs. No gating required; both short and long p95 remain inside SLOs with ~25–30% headroom for growth.

2) Include an operational policy appendix: prewarm time (90s), KV cache priming for expected heavy-request keys, and token-based throttles for billing-event buckets.

3) Ask GraniteAI to confirm acceptable worst-case long-path p95 if they prefer Option A (trade-off clarity required).

4) Attach the workload CSV and the 3-scenario TCO (we'll finalize figures before the call).

Amit/Lucia — can you confirm whether gating (soft-disconnects for non-critical long jobs) is acceptable as an operational compromise for the POC? If yes, we will recommend Option A and show cost savings vs Option B.

I'll finalize slides and the commit language; Lauren, Ben — please review the TCO numbers I'll add (draft in Drive).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
